items.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...there are some like Roy Haynes… [INTERVIEWEE] I don’t think there is.

ctx.x: I can’t say that. We can stop for a minute.
Ready to pick it up? Kimery: We are ready.

Okay, so before we had to briefly interrupt I was asking about, again certain areas developed a style, and in this case comparing it to the Boston school of drumming. But I was just wondering if there are any other drummers in that area who might have either inspired Elvin or might have another style, I’m just trying to get a sense ‘cause Elvin’s style, as you valorize it, is the uniqueness of somebody’s individual voice. And Elvin’s voice, we can’t trace, I mean, there’s some like Roy Haynes…

items.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That’s when I started doing things with Kenny Burrell a little bit then. The Vanguard – I think we did a record down there.

ctx.x: So in order to facilitate your family life, you would just take gigs here in the New York area? You would minimize your touring?
Yes. I had been around a lot. Yeah. That’s when I started doing things with Kenny Burrell a little bit then. The Vanguard – I think we did a record down there. And the Monk thing . . .
